source.title: Feature learning in neural networks and kernel machines that recursively learn features
source.authors: Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan; Daniel Beaglehole; Parthe Pandit; Mikhail Belkin

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test-accuracy changes during training after training accuracy is already near 100%, a conceptual test of coexistence between fitting and generalization. Its main focus is feature learning, not random-label memorization.
record.gate_note: The STL-10 grokking experiment reports training and test accuracy as training continues past near-perfect training accuracy. Other generalization-related numbers concern RFM performance, feature perturbations, or comparisons and do not measure the claim versions' specified outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature learning, grokking and RFM performance, but none of V1–V8. Continued training after near-perfect training accuracy does not test V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization. Its width sweep measures feature-matrix correlations rather than V2's test error beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the grokking result, but only that result. The paper's broader conclusion is that average gradient outer products characterize feature learning in fully connected networks and enable Recursive Feature Machines with strong tabular benchmark performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines feature learning and grokking on a deliberately modified, class-imbalanced STL-10 subset; it does not reproduce the claim's random-label memorization or generalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration changes test accuracy in the modified STL-10 grokking experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: On modified, imbalanced STL-10, test accuracy increases from roughly 80% to 99.38% during continued training after near-perfect training accuracy, alongside learning the class-correlated star cue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued training can improve held-out accuracy after near-perfect training accuracy through delayed feature learning.

record.problems: The grokking result uses a deliberately modified dataset with a class-correlated star cue and a small, imbalanced training subset, so it does not establish the claim's natural-label result. No uncertainty estimate is stated for this result.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported generalization or accuracy results concern feature-matrix correlations, feature masking, RFM performance, or benchmark comparisons and do not measure any listed claim version. No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural labels under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Image generalization of convolutional versus fully connected networks, including the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: R1's cannot_determine state concerns its relevance to the listed versions; the grokking accuracy increase itself is explicitly reported. Feature pruning removes input coordinates, not memorized training examples, and therefore does not test V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold with test error as the outcome.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison testing image generalization.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples or comparison with random removal.

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer fully connected ReLU network
rows.stage_stated: trained with Adam; training duration varied
rows.operation_detail: continued training after reaching near 100% training accuracy on modified STL-10

conditions.value: modified STL-10; 553 training examples, with 500 airplanes and 53 trucks; balanced test set with 800 examples per class
80% of 553 samples used for training and 20% for validation
Adam, learning rate 10^-4, batch size equal to dataset size

rows.baseline: roughly 80% when training accuracy is near 100%
rows.note: The experiment adds class-correlated star pixels to a small, imbalanced training subset; it is not a natural-label generalization test. Training accuracy is described as near 100%, not exact zero error.
rows.check: The reported increase from roughly 80% to 99.38% is accurate, but it cannot establish any listed version. The 553 examples comprise training and validation combined; 80% are used for training. The labels identify natural classes, augmented with an artificial class-correlated star cue; the missing random-label comparison, rather than artificial cues alone, prevents a V1 test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
